course_description: This course provides a short introduction to research in physics. Students choose a topic and a supervisor, and submit a written report by the end of semester.

restrictions: Permission required to enrol. Please contact the School of Mathematics and Physics (smp.student@uq.edu.au).

timetable:
Additional timetable information
This is a research project course, and as such there are no regularly scheduled contact hours. As a #2-unit subject, you are expected to contribute 10 hrs per week towards your research project.
You should have regular meetings as agreed with your supervisor. Typically this is thirty minutes to one hour per week. You may find the provided document "ResearchProjectExpectations.pdf" on Blackboard useful in setting the expectations for roles in these regular meetings.
You need to map out a program of work with your supervisor in the early weeks of your project as background to your project plan (due end of 2nd week). Ideally this should occur prior to semester start.
course_aims: The aim of the research project is to develop the research skills of the student by carrying out a small project at the cutting edge of a specialised area of physics.ﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Be able to plan, develop and carry out an independent research project.
Obtain an in-depth knowledge of the specific topic area through a thorough literature review.
Develop research skills and be able to locate and use information sources.
Present results of research in a written thesis.

assessment_details.title: Outline of research
assessment_details.task_description: Write a research proposal of up to, but not more than, one page, describing the background and aims of your project. Make sure you include the project title, your name, and that of your supervisor. Please show this to your supervisor for feedback before you submit it. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Submit via Blackboard through the assessment item.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
A timely submission of the research outline is required in order to receive feedback and to ensure that the project can be successfully completed during semester. Hence an extension beyond 7 days is not possible.
See ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENT INFORMATION for extension and deferred examination information relating to this assessment item.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
Students who are unable to arrange a supervisor and complete the outline of research by the end of Week 2 should consider withdrawing from the course. Please contact the Course Coordinator for advice.

assessment_details.title: Weekly project reports
assessment_details.task_description: Students are requested to meet weekly with their supervisors and provide an update on progress. This should be summarised in a written format electronically and shared with your supervisor each week for review. The report should include the following: Last week’s goals and progress to date Goals for the following week Brief summary of what is discussed Students may also include any relevant data as they see fit. Please append each weekly summaries into the same shared document, so that at the end of the semester there is a continuous record of progress on the project in a single document. If the meeting cannot be held due to unavailability, then this should be noted. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Oral defense
assessment_details.task_description: During the exam period after you hand in your report you will attend in person an oral defense with the examiners and your project supervisor. The course coordinator may also attend. You will need to discuss a suitable date and venue with your project supervisor, examiners, and course coordinator. Examiners or supervisors may join the exam via video conferencing if necessary. The expert examiner shall lead the examination, with the supervisor (and course coordinator, if they attend) as observers. The oral defense is designed to complement the written report by providing an authentic assessment of each student’s understanding of, and intellectual contribution to, the research project. It gives students an opportunity to explain their work, present results and their interpretation, and respond to questions from examiners with different levels of familiarity with the research area. The defense also supports academic integrity by allowing the examiners to confirm that the student understands and can independently discuss the work presented in the report. This is particularly important because the use of generative artificial intelligence and other forms of external assistance in the preparation of written work can be difficult to identify or control. The oral defense does not assess whether a particular tool was used; rather, it assesses the student’s demonstrated ownership, understanding, critical judgement, and ability to communicate the submitted work. This assessment item will be audio-visually recorded and retained in accordance with University requirements. This assessment item is not eligible for a remark due to it being independently marked by two examiners. Read full task description Hide full task description
